cost: B bytes,C scalars,T tokens: scanning O(B), NFC O(C+combining-order work), units O(C) time/O(C) slice pointers; tokenize stores O(B+T). Pathological combining sequences may increase normalization work.
description: norm filters Hebrew accent/joiner set and optionally points, then NFC. units slices original UTF-8 at each noncombining scalar; tokenize NFC-normalizes, splits whitespace/punctuation/maqaf and groups after closing marks plus paragraph markers. thin chooses points by raw-byte hash and scalar position.
forward: norm filters Hebrew accent/joiner set and optionally points, then NFC. units slices original UTF-8 at each noncombining scalar; tokenize NFC-normalizes, splits whitespace/punctuation/maqaf and groups after closing marks plus paragraph markers. thin chooses points by raw-byte hash and scalar position.
inverse: norm cannot retain selected accent/joiner characters; unpointed cannot retain selected points. tokenize cannot cut apostrophes inside a word merely because is_mark recognizes a standalone apostrophe.

A normalized string admits all filtered-mark insertions and canonically equivalent original strings. Token sentences additionally lose whitespace spelling; units plus original slices reconstruct exact bytes, unlike normalization.
limitations: Finite supplied-input checks only; no corpus, training, external annotator, GPU, throughput or semantic-understanding claim. Allocation exhaustion and malformed arbitrary model arithmetic are not exhaustively exercised. No useful numerical surrogate is implemented; future caps may only be 1/2/5/10% with a declared metric.
state: Units partition exact original bytes; coordinates are neither Unicode scalar positions nor bytes. Point removal preserves nonpoint/nonaccent scalars before NFC. Leading marks form their own first unit. Hash overflow is explicit wrapping.
